articles.title: Northampton 28-14 Gloucester: Saints come from behind to beat in-form Gloucester
articles.summary: Late tries from George Hendy and Rory Hutchison gift Northampton Saints victory over stubborn Gloucester.
articles.body:
Tries: Pearson, Langdon, Hendy, Hutchinson Cons: Belleau 4

Northampton Saints scored 28 unanswered points to come from behind and overcome a stubborn Gloucester 28-14 at DPD Stadium at Franklin's Gardens.

But England boss Steve Borthwick will be concerned after scrum-half Alex Mitchell was forced off with a hamstring injury during the first half.

Gloucester had the better of the opening exchanges with tries from Max Llewellyn and Will Joseph opening up a 14 point lead, before Tom Pearson responded for Saints.

Curtis Langdon's effort on the verge of half-time brought the scores level, but it took until the final quarter for Saints to really seize control of the game.

George Hendy added a third try after a pinpoint pass from Anthony Belleau before Rory Hutchinson's late score put the game beyond the visitors.

Victory moves Northampton up to third in the table, level on points with Gloucester in second as the Prem takes a four-week break.

Cokanasiga scores twice as Bath overcome Sale

Second-half blitz helps Saracens beat Newcastle

Quins claim victory at Exeter in nine-try nailbiter

In the misty conditions, it was the visitors who struck first.

Attacking in the Saints' 22, the returning Seb Atkinson released George Barton who offloaded to Llewellyn to dot down over the whitewash.

Saints then suffered another blow as Mitchell left the field eight days before England face Australia in the Nations Championship.

After being repeatedly repelled by Northampton's defence, Gloucester then scored again. Following a well executed set-piece move, Hendy was unable to contain Joseph, who stumbled over the line to add the Cherry and Whites' second.

Northampton desperately needed some attacking emphasis and finally found it through Pearson.

With Gloucester penalised in their own half, Saints kicked for the corner. The resulting rolling maul had seemingly come to a halt, but Langdon managed to pop the ball up to the flanker who crashed over at short range.

Saints then claimed a second in similar circumstances right before half-time. Another driving line-out was initially kept out by Gloucester before it splintered, allowing Langdon to dive over.

Missing the impetus of injured fly-half Fin Smith , Saints continued to struggle in attack after the restart with another promising opportunity snuffed out by a Joseph interception.

With both defences on top, the game needed a moment of real quality and eventually received it from Belleau.

With the Gloucester defence narrow, the fly-half played a perfect looped pass to Hendy who dived over in the corner to give Saints the lead.

Hutchinson then added a bonus point fourth, the replacement centre exploiting Gloucester's press defence with a quick step to force his way over the line.

Gloucester continued pressing until the end but were unable to breach the Saints defence, recording only their second loss of the season.

'We were alive to opportunities' - reaction

Northampton Saints head coach Sam Vesty told BBC Radio Northampton:

"[It was] a really satisfying win, a real contest of attack and defence, where both defences were tested but stood up.

"We started doing a lot of things better with 10 minutes to go in the first half. We moved off the ball better, created opportunities and we got that try just before half-time which is always a good time to score.

"In a game where defences are strong, you have to be pretty ruthless and we were alive to the opportunities, which was good to see."

"He felt something in his hamstring, we can't know more than that. It may not be too bad but then nobody who pulls their hamstring thinks it's bad."

Gloucester head coach George Skivington told BBC Radio Gloucestershire:

"We came out of the blocks well, attacked the game, but we just weren't accurate enough especially at the back-end of the first-half.

"We had some real opportunities and could've come in 14 or even 21 nil up, but we gave away a couple of penalties, they scored too easily and suddenly it was 14 all.

"We didn't get the launches and the ball through the hands the way we wanted to. The boys stayed in the fight, kept trying, but a lot of our play was scrappy balls, picking balls off the floor and Saints took their opportunities really well.

"There will be some good learnings here."

Northampton: Pater; Sleightholme, Freeman, Dingwall (c), Hendy; Belleau, Mitchell; Iyogun, Langdon, Kundiona; Coles, Prowse, Kemeny, Pearson, Chick.

Replacements: Smith, Fischetti, Neculai, Van Der Mescht, Lockett, Pollock, Weimann, Hutchinson.

Gloucester: Barton; Joseph, Llewellyn, S Atkinson (c), W Knight; C Atkinson, Englefield; Rapava Ruskin, Blake, Fasogbon; Kleyn, Clark, Thomas, Gwynne, Clement.

Replacements: Lake, Bleuler, C Knight, Trenholm, Morgan, Ludlow, Robson, Redshaw.

articles.title: Ospreys 0-26 Cardiff: Two-try Tom Bowen provides URC derby success
articles.summary: Cardiff lift themselves back into the top half of the United Rugby Championship (URC) by defeating Ospreys 26-0 in a scrappy Welsh derby at St Helen's.
articles.body:
Tries: Bowen 2, Adams, Howe Cons: Evans 2, Sheedy

Cardiff lifted themselves back into the top half of the United Rugby Championship (URC) by defeating Ospreys 26-0 in a scrappy Welsh derby at St Helen's.

Two tries from wing Tom Bowen and further scores from Josh Adams and hooker Tom Howe sealed the away bonus-point success against a lacklustre home side in Swansea.

Ospreys previously failed to score in a 23-0 defeat against Munster in October 2024.

Cardiff centre Steffan Emanuel was a creative influence and should prove an option for Wales if they pick up any midfield injuries next month.

His contribution was a shining light in a dour derby played in front of a 5,592 sell-out, with the occasion marred by the continued whistle of referee Ben Breakspear.

It was the second game at the revamped St Helen's ground after the opening Ospreys victory against Dragons .

The URC takes a break for five weeks, with the Nations Championship staged in November. Cardiff finish the first league block in seventh and Ospreys in ninth.

While there has been renewed talk of an Anglo-Welsh league this week , the URC match schedulers should reflect on their fixture choices with a significant Welsh derby staged a week before an international campaign and shorn of the Wales stars.

Adams was the only Welsh region-based member of Steve Tandy's squad to be sent out for game time prior to the Nations Championship.

Cardiff were without their six other Wales squad members, including Rhys Barratt, hooker Liam Belcher, lock Teddy Williams and back-row trio Alex Mann, James Botham and Taine Basham.

Full-back Tom Rogers, fly-half Dan Edwards, scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams and loose-head prop Gareth Thomas sat out for Ospreys.

With fly-half Lawson Creighton a late withdrawal because of a groin injury, Harri Wilde, who was on loan at Ospreys from Cardiff, started against his parent club. Wilde formed a third-choice half-back partnership with Luke Davies.

Cardiff enjoyed all the early pressure and were rewarded with a walk in for wing Bowen.

Ospreys appeared to have responded when prop Steffan Thomas was driven over, but after the try was initially given, the television match official (TMO) disallowed it after it was deemed that Cardiff scrum-half Johan Mulder had prevented the grounding.

Cardiff weathered the Ospreys attack and produced a well-worked scrum set-piece move which saw Bowen sprint over for his second.

Emanuel almost created a third try with a fine break and kick, but the Ospreys defence scrambled back and held firm.

Following a Dan Thomas turnover penalty, Emanuel turned creator with his deft kick being latched onto by Adams.

Ospreys suffered another blow when flanker Ross Moriarty suffered a nasty head injury and was replaced by Morgan Morse as dominant Cardiff took a deserved 19-0 half-time lead.

Ospreys started the second half with scrummaging superiority, with Cardiff replacing props Keiron Assiratti and Danny Southworth with international duo Scott Sio and Javan Sebastian.

Adams received treatment for a knee injury but was able to continue before Ospreys co-captain Sam Parry was held up over the Cardiff line.

Cardiff were warned for persistent penalties, and the frustrations of the Ospreys players with how the officials were interpreting the breakdown could be heard.

Cardiff repelled the Ospreys' defence with teenage replacement hooker Howe winning a crucial turnover penalty as the visitors‘ dynamic defence kept Ospreys at bay.

Howe gained his reward as Cardiff demonstrated a clinical approach, with the 18-year-old securing the bonus-point try after being driven over.

It was the only score as Emanuel denied Keelan Giles in the dying seconds with a wonderful covering tackle to complete the impressive victory.

The woeful second half was short on quality, but Cardiff's players, coaches and supporters will not care as they secured maximum points against an Ospreys side that looked devoid of attacking ideas.

Ospreys: Hopkins; Morgan, Watkin (co-capt), K Williams, Giles; Wilde, L Davies; S Thomas, Parry (co-capt), Botha, Ratti, Smith, Wright, Moriarty, M Morris.

Replacements: Daniel, C Jones, Warren, Sutton, Morse, H Williams, S Jac Jones, Boshoff.

Cardiff: Young; Adams, Malan, Emanuel, Bowen; J Evans, Mulder; Southworth, Hughes, Assiratti, McNally (capt), Thornton, Paea, Thomas, Lawrence.

Replacements: Howe, Sio, Sebastian, Manz, de la Rua, A Davies, Sheedy, Darwin-Lewis.

Assistant referees: Carwyn Sion & Marc Caudle (Wales)
